installation.note: killall is part of the psmisc package, which may not be installed by default on all systems

overview.summary: The killall command terminates processes by name, rather than by process ID (PID). It's useful for killing multiple instances of a program or when you know the process name but not the PID. Use with caution as it can terminate all processes matching the name.
when_to_use: Kill all instances of a program by name
Terminate processes when you know the name but not PID
Clean up multiple processes of the same name
Force quit applications from command line

syntax.description: killall sends a signal (default: SIGTERM) to all processes matching the specified name. The process name must match exactly (case-sensitive by default).

misconceptions.title: Kills all processes
misconceptions.misconception: killall kills all processes on the system
misconceptions.reality: killall kills only processes matching the specified name. The name 'killall' is misleading - it kills 'all' processes with that name, not all processes.
misconceptions.tip: Always specify a process name. Use 'killall -l' to list available signals

misconceptions.title: Same as kill
misconceptions.misconception: killall and kill are the same
misconceptions.reality: kill requires a PID, killall uses process names. killall is more convenient when you know the program name.
misconceptions.tip: Use 'kill' with PID, 'killall' with process name

common_pitfalls.description: killall terminates ALL processes matching the name, not just one
common_pitfalls.solution: Use 'kill' with specific PID if you only want to kill one process, or use 'pkill' with more filtering options

common_pitfalls.description: Cannot kill processes owned by other users
common_pitfalls.solution: Use 'sudo' to kill processes owned by other users, or use '-u' to specify user

common_pitfalls.description: Process names are case-sensitive by default
common_pitfalls.solution: Use '-I' option for case-insensitive matching, or ensure exact case match
Use 'ps aux | grep processname' to find exact process name, or use '-r' for regex matching

related_commands.description: kill terminates processes by PID rather than name
pkill also kills by name but with more pattern matching options
ps lists processes to find names or PIDs before killing
pgrep finds process IDs by name before using kill

best_practices: Use '-i' (interactive) option to prevent accidental kills
Try normal termination first (default SIGTERM) before using -9 (SIGKILL)
Use '-v' to verify processes were killed
Check process names with 'ps' before killing
Use '-u' to limit kills to specific user's processes
Be cautious - killall affects ALL matching processes
performance_tips: Use '-w' to wait for processes to die before continuing scripts
Regex matching (-r) can be slower for many processes

additional_notes.warning: killall can terminate multiple processes. Use with caution, especially with common process names.
additional_notes.signal: Default signal is SIGTERM (15). Use -9 for SIGKILL only when necessary as it cannot be caught or ignored.
